facts.fact: Techweez reports that schools entered pathway, subject-combination and senior-school choices against each learner's record on KEMIS for nearly 1.2 million Grade 9 learners, KEMIS being the required platform for the 2026 Grade 10 selection, in an exercise due to close on 11 September 2026.

Techweez states that KEMIS is built to pull together data from early childhood education through to university, where NEMIS mostly served basic education; no date is given, so the publication date is used.
Techweez states that KEMIS is funded through the World Bank-backed Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning Programme; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

Techweez states that the Ministry of Education describes KEMIS as a government-led project with other state agencies, development partners and unnamed technology providers, and has not named the contractor or published the agreements; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Education Principal Secretary told the Public Accounts Committee in late August 2026 that the latest capitation disbursement used neither NEMIS nor KEMIS but manually verified data, because KEMIS was not yet complete.
KEMIS became the required platform for the 2026 Grade 10 selection exercise covering nearly 1.2 million Grade 9 learners, closing on 11 September 2026.

During the Grade 10 selection in September 2026 schools reported failed logins, slow responses, submissions that did not save and learner records showing the previous Grade 9 cohort on KEMIS, and the Ministry sent field officers to monitor while technical teams stabilised it; the number of schools affected is not given.
